title: Meeting A: Initial Discovery - Legal Directory Portal
transcript:
Alex (Consultant): Thanks for meeting today, Sarah. Let's walk through your core objectives for the Texas Legal Directory launch.

Sarah (Client): Thanks Alex. We currently have an older website that costs too much to maintain. We need three major things for this first launch.
First, we have an Excel sheet with about 450 legal practice categories—things like Criminal Defense, Corporate Tax, Patent Law, and Family Mediation. We need those imported into a clean category hierarchy so attorneys can list their specialties.

Alex (Consultant): Got it. Brilliant Directories supports top-level, sub-level, and sub-sub categories, and we can import that via CSV. What about member payments?

Sarah (Client): Yes! We want attorneys to sign up online and pay either monthly or annually. We want to use Stripe, but our corporate counsel says we must have 3D Secure and SCA compliance because we have international law partners.

Alex (Consultant): Completely understood. Stripe SCA is natively supported in Brilliant Directories. What about visitor search?

Sarah (Client): The search needs to let people search by practice area and zip code with a radius filter. And we also want homeowners or business clients to submit a lead inquiry form, and have the system automatically match and route the lead to up to 3 attorneys in that county.

Alex (Consultant): Auto-matching leads by category and location is a built-in feature. Anything else on your wishlist?

Sarah (Client): We were thinking of adding a custom 1-on-1 video consultation booking calendar directly on attorney profiles where clients can book a 30-minute Zoom slot.

Alex (Consultant): That custom calendar would require custom React/API development since it's not a native setting. We will estimate that as a separate task. What is your timeline and budget?

Sarah (Client): We are aiming for a launch in 4 weeks, with a target budget around $3,500.

title: Meeting B: Discovery - Fitness Network E-Commerce & Subscriptions
transcript:
Alex (Consultant): Hi Dave, let's explore the requirements for FitPro Hub.

Dave (Client): Hi Alex. We are building a directory for certified fitness trainers and gyms. Aside from directory listings, we want to monetize through digital workout guides—PDF downloads that members can purchase for $19 each.

Alex (Consultant): Brilliant Directories has a digital products add-on that handles downloadable assets and single-charge transactions through Stripe.

Dave (Client): Great. We also have two membership tiers: Free Trainer and Pro Certified ($39/mo). Can trainers upgrade directly from their member dashboard?

Alex (Consultant): Yes, self-service plan upgrades are native. What about your accounting integrations?

Dave (Client): Our CPA uses QuickBooks Online. We need member signups and payment receipts pushed to QuickBooks automatically.

Alex (Consultant): We can set up an outbound webhook from Brilliant Directories to Zapier or Make, which will sync customer invoice records directly to QuickBooks in real-time.

Dave (Client): Perfect. We also want a dynamic pricing calculator on our homepage where visitors slide a bar with how many clients they train to see their estimated monthly earnings.

Alex (Consultant): That interactive slider calculator is a custom frontend widget. We can build that with custom JavaScript and embed it into your homepage widget manager.

Dave (Client): Excellent, our target launch is in 5 weeks with a budget around $4,000.

title: Meeting C: Follow-Up & Scope Revisions (Revises Meeting A)
transcript:
Alex (Consultant): Hi Sarah, welcome back. We reviewed our initial scope from Meeting A. How are things looking on your side?

Sarah (Client): Hi Alex. We met with our advisory board and we have some important adjustments to the plan.
First, to keep our initial phase simple and save on costs, we decided to completely DROP the automated lead distribution feature. We will handle client inquiries manually for the first 6 months. So please remove lead auto-matching from the scope.

Alex (Consultant): Understood. Removing automated lead matching will reduce configuration and testing effort.

Sarah (Client): Second, on our search results page, our board wants an enhanced mobile filter bar where clients can toggle 'Available on Weekends' and 'Free Initial Consultation' pills right above the search cards.

Alex (Consultant): That's a great addition. We can build that custom mobile filter widget with lightweight CSS and JavaScript.

Sarah (Client): Third, we also decided to postpone the custom Zoom booking calendar for Phase 2, so please exclude that from this quote as well.

Alex (Consultant): Got it. That removes about 20 hours of custom calendar integration.

Sarah (Client): Here's the big ask though: our investors asked if we can also get native iOS and Android apps submitted to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store for our directory. Can you guys just include full native mobile app development in this contract for like an extra $500?

Alex (Consultant): Sarah, native iOS and Android apps with App Store submission are an entirely separate mobile architecture. That cannot be included in a $500 add-on and falls outside our web directory scope. We will flag that as an explicit out-of-scope item and provide a separate mobile contract if your board wants to pursue it.

Sarah (Client): Fair enough, please quote it separately. Also, our launch date has moved up—we now need to launch in 2 weeks instead of 4 weeks because of a state bar convention.
